chapter_note: Chapter 46 is a remarkably pure example of the cosmological substrate. It consists of a structured sequence of "beforehand, before X happened/manifested, they sent/appointed Y" — a pre-emptive ordainment catalog covering: the Third Ambassador (against night/day mixture), the Father of Life adorning ships, the Judge (before Sin reigned), Christ the blessed (before Error manifested), the stars and spheres (before bodies were slain), the releasers (before cosmos is released), and the Great Builder / First Architect (before the New Aeon is summoned). The whole chapter follows a single architectonic pattern: pre-cosmic ordering of cosmic offices. The fatigue score reports later-layer drift, but on close reading this is artifact: the "drift" in second half tracks substrate cosmic structures (stars, spheres, Aeon, Builder, angels) that the vocabulary counter mis-flags as ecclesial. The polemic flags around segs 17-21 (Christ cutting Error, doctrines) are part of the same cosmological pattern of pre-emptive sendings — Christ here is a cosmic figure in the ordainment series, not anti-heretical polemic per se. Heavy damage (59.5%) means many segments are fragmentary but their pattern is clear.
